Actionable feedback from Copilot:
- [e2e/testutil/repo.go](/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli_experiments_2/e2e/testutil/repo.go#L178): writing `~/.gemini/acknowledgments/agents.json` mutates real user/CI state and is not restored. Suggestion: capture original contents and restore or delete with `t.Cleanup`, or isolate Gemini with a test-specific `HOME`.
- [e2e/testutil/repo.go](/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli_experiments_2/e2e/testutil/repo.go#L195): the JSON is keyed by `repoDir`, which is a temp path, so entries will accumulate over time unless cleaned up.
- [e2e/testutil/repo.go](/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli_experiments_2/e2e/testutil/repo.go#L184): the code assumes `agents.json` always matches `map[string]map[string]string`; if Gemini changes schema or the file is corrupted, the test fails before startup. Suggestion: parse more defensively or use isolated config state.

If you want, I can patch this now and make the helper hermetic.
yes, make the helper hermetic
I’m updating the Gemini acknowledgment helper to stop leaking state into the real home directory and to clean up after itself between test runs.

I’ve got the helper code. Before editing, I’m checking whether Gemini session startup already supports a per-test config directory; if it does, isolating that would be cleaner than mutating the real home file at all.

The current helper can restore the file, but parallel E2E runs would still fight over the same `~/.gemini` path. I’m switching Gemini’s E2E config to a per-test home directory instead, then pointing the helper at that isolated location.

I found a cleaner fix than backup/restore: Gemini’s E2E path can use an isolated per-repo home, similar to how Cursor and Codex isolate state. I’m wiring the helper and Gemini agent to use that instead of `~/.gemini`.

I’m editing both the test helper and the Gemini agent wrapper now: repo setup will seed a private Gemini home, and both prompt and tmux paths will run against that isolated home instead of the user profile.
The code changes are in place. I’m formatting and doing a compile-level test pass on the touched E2E packages to catch any integration mistakes before I hand this back.

I made the Gemini helper hermetic by moving it off the real `~/.gemini` state entirely.

[e2e/testutil/repo.go](/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli_experiments_2/e2e/testutil/repo.go#L159) now creates a per-repo Gemini home, seeds `settings.json` and `acknowledgments/agents.json` there, and cleans that directory up with `t.Cleanup`. It no longer reads or writes the user’s real home, and it handles malformed existing JSON defensively instead of failing the test setup.

[e2e/agents/gemini.go](/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli_experiments_2/e2e/agents/gemini.go#L54) now runs both prompt mode and tmux sessions with `HOME` pointed at that isolated test home, so the helper and Gemini CLI use the same private config. I also removed the old bootstrap behavior that wrote to the real profile.

what's the command to run real gemini e2e? and can I do this localy from an auth perspective?
I’m checking the E2E docs and Gemini agent wrapper so I can give you the exact command and the local auth expectations, not just the CI path.

Use:

```bash
mise run test:e2e --agent gemini-cli
```

To run a single test or subset:

```bash
mise run test:e2e --agent gemini-cli TestInteractive
```

From a local auth perspective: yes, you can run it locally, but after the hermetic change it should be treated as API-key based auth. The Gemini E2E wrapper now points `HOME` at an isolated per-test directory, so it will not reuse your real `~/.gemini` OAuth/login state.

What you need locally:
- `gemini` installed on `PATH`
- `GEMINI_API_KEY` exported in your shell

Example:

```bash
export GEMINI_API_KEY=...
mise run test:e2e --agent gemini-cli
```

Useful flags while debugging:

```bash
E2E_KEEP_REPOS=1 mise run test:e2e --agent gemini-cli TestInteractive
E2E_TIMEOUT=4m mise run test:e2e --agent gemini-cli
```

If you want, I can also point you at the smallest Gemini E2E test to run first.
I wonder now: the json parsing part, would we not want to know this changed? Like I feel the failure might be more interesting then keeping it working because we parse not so strict?

Yes. For this case, I think silent tolerance is the weaker choice.

There are really two separate concerns:

1. Hermeticity
2. Schema drift detection

Hermeticity should be unconditional. The test must not touch real `~/.gemini`.

Schema drift is different. If `agents.json` in the isolated test home is malformed, that is usually a harness bug or an upstream Gemini behavior change, and failing loudly is useful. Since we now fully own that file in the test home, there is much less reason to be permissive.

So the stricter design is probably better:
- create isolated Gemini home
- write the exact schema we expect
- if later reads fail to parse, fail the test
- optionally make the error explicit, like “Gemini acknowledgments schema changed”

The earlier “parse loosely” advice made more sense when the code was mutating a real user-managed file. In that world, robustness matters because local machine state may be arbitrary. Now that the file is test-owned, strict parsing is a better signal.

I’d lean toward changing this back to strict parsing in [e2e/testutil/repo.go](/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli_experiments_2/e2e/testutil/repo.go), while keeping the isolated-home part. If you want, I can make that adjustment now.
